title: Why learners privilege word-order over case-marking: A cross-linguistic meta-analysis, new data from Estonian, Finnish and Polish, and a discriminative learning model.
title_zh: 学习者为何更偏重词序而非格标记：跨语言元分析、爱沙尼亚语、芬兰语和波兰语的新数据及判别学习模型
abstract: Language acquisition is one of the crowning achievements of our species; though a long-standing and unresolved question is why many learners struggle with a particular core and fundamental sentence type. In English, a two-participant sentence like The dog chased the cat can mean only one thing. But in many languages worldwide, the meaning of the sentence can be flipped (e.g., to "the cat chased the dog") even while the word-order stays the same, by the use of case-marked nouns (e.g., cat + NOMINATIVE, dog + ACCUSATIVE). First (Study 1), we confirm using meta-analysis that, across 21 languages, children show a significant disadvantage for noncanonical ("flipped") versus canonical ("unflipped") sentences (Cohen's d = 0.69, SE = 0.09). Second (Study 2), we demonstrate with a new comprehension study of 3- to 6-year-old native learners of Estonian (N = 87), Finnish (N = 83), and Polish (N = 82) that this effect is not due to (a) lack of knowledge of individual inflected words, (b) lack of linguistic context, (c) use of still pictures as opposed to animations, or (d) a focus on relatively young children. Third (Study 3), we show that this effect falls naturally out of a simple discriminative-learning model, in which the cue of case-marking struggles to compete with the more frequently available cue of word-order to predict which noun (e.g., dog and cat) is the AGENT (e.g., the chaser), and which the PATIENT (e.g., the one chased). Together, these findings demonstrate that languages which, on the surface, appear to be very different are learned in a similar way: by discriminating cues to meaning. abstract_zh: 语言习得是人类最杰出的成就之一；然而一个长期存在且未解的问题是，为什么许多学习者在掌握某种核心且基本的句型时会遇到困难。在英语中，像“The dog chased the cat”这样的两参与者句子只能有一种含义。但在世界上许多语言中，即使词序保持不变，句子的意义也可以被颠倒（例如“the cat chased the dog”），这通过使用格标记名词实现（如cat + NOMINATIVE，dog + ACCUSATIVE）。第一项（研究1），我们通过元分析确认，在21种语言中，儿童在非典型（“颠倒”）句子与典型（“未颠倒”）句子之间存在显著劣势（Cohen's d = 0.69，SE = 0.09）。第二项（研究2），我们通过对爱沙尼亚语（N = 87）、芬兰语（N = 83）和波兰语（N = 82）的3至6岁母语学习者进行新的理解研究，证明这一效应并非由于（a）缺乏对单个屈折词的知识，（b）缺乏语言情境，（c）使用静态图片而非动画，或（d）聚焦于相对年幼的儿童所致。第三项（研究3），我们展示该效应自然地源自一个简单的判别学习模型，在该模型中，格标记的提示难以与更频繁出现的词序提示竞争，以预测哪个名词（如dog和cat）是AGENT（如追逐者），哪个是PATIENT（如被追逐者）。综上所述，这些发现表明，表面上看似非常不同的语言在学习方式上是相似的：通过区分意义的线索来学习。（PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA，保留所有权利）
